quadrant.comment: Begin quadrantChart at its exact detector prefix; a statement may touch the header. quadrant.md#detection: The header may be the whole text. quadrant.md#detection: On the line of the header, the first statement may follow the header, after spaces, after a tab, or with nothing between them, and so may a `;`, a comment, or a directive: `quadrantChart title T`, `quadrantChart;title T`, and `quadrantChartA: [0.3, 0.6]` are accepted.

patterns.comment: Read point styles after the coordinate list, keeping directives in their opening gap. quadrant.md#points: A point is a name, a class name after `:::` or none, and two coordinates in brackets, with styles after the `]` or none. quadrant.md#points: The styles are separated by `,`, with whitespace around it or not, and may follow the `]` with no space. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a local description block with case-insensitive keyword and Notation whitespace, keeping inline percent pairs as text. quadrant.md#accessibility-values: `accDescr`, whitespace, and `{` enter the description block context, which reads the whitespace after the `{` and then every character up to the next `}` as a `description-block-text` unit, reads the `}` as a `}` unit, and leaves; the whitespace before the `}` is part of the text. When only whitespace lies between the `{` and the `}`, there is no `description-block-text` unit. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a description text run, stopping before a common comment or the closing brace. quadrant.md#accessibility-values: The text may hold line feeds, `#`, `;`, quotes, keywords, and `%%`; a CRLF or a lone CR in it is a line feed. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read the local accessibility line forms with Notation whitespace and literal inline percent pairs. quadrant.md#accessibility-values: `accTitle` and `:` enter the accessibility title context, and `accDescr` and `:` the accessibility description context. Each reads the whitespace after the `:`, line feeds included, and then the rest of the line as an `acc-title-text` or an `acc-description-text` unit, and leaves. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a bounded title and its remaining line, including punctuation and percent pairs. quadrant.md#the-title-context: `title` enters the title context, which reads the rest of the line as a `title-text` unit and leaves; the unit is empty when the line ends after the keyword. quadrant.md#the-title-context: Every character up to the line feed is a character of the title: a `;`, a `#`, `%%` and what follows it, quotes, a colon, keywords, and a text that looks like a point. So `title T; quadrant-1 A` is the title `T; quadrant-1 A`, and `title: [0.3, 0.6]` is a title. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a class definition's element name and its properties, with exactly one diagram whitespace character on each side of the name. quadrant.md#classes: A class definition is `classDef`, one whitespace character, the name, one whitespace character, and the styles of a point. quadrant.md#classes: Two whitespace characters before the name are rejected, while whitespace after the second one belongs to the first style. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read axis and quadrant keywords, including a keyword touching its text. quadrant.md#the-statement-context: `x-axis`, `y-axis`, `quadrant-1` to `quadrant-4`, and the header need nothing after them: `x-axisL`, `x-axis1`, `x-axis_x`, and `x-axisé` are the x axis with a text, and `quadrant-11` is `quadrant-1` with the text `1`, while `x-axis-x` and `quadrant-1-x` are a keyword and a text that starts with a dash, which is rejected.
patterns.name: keyword.control.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read an axis arrow as one relation operator. quadrant.md#axes: The arrow is two dashes or more and `>`, with spaces around it or not: `L-->R` and `L ---> R` have the texts `L` and `R`, while `L -> R`, `L -- > R`, a second arrow, an arrow with no text before it, and the keyword alone are rejected, and so are a tab between the keyword and the text and a tab around the arrow, which are `space` units.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arrow.mermaid

patterns.comment: Reuse the shared HTML tag reader for converted attribute quotes. common.md#html-attribute-quotes: The lexer reads the two `"` of each quoted value as `'`.

Read an entity as label text, preserving its directives. quadrant.md#units-and-contexts: An entity is read as its placeholder (see [Entities](../common.md#entities)), which is made of characters outside ASCII, so it is a character of every text, name, title, and accessibility text, and of the name of a class of `classDef`, while the class name of a point and a style take no placeholder: `#f00;` in a style is an entity, so `A: [0.3, 0.6] color: #f00;` is rejected, while `A: [0.3, 0.6] color: #f00 ;` has the colour `#f00`.
patterns.name: string.unquoted.mermaid

patterns.comment: Reuse the shared markdown delimiter reader; invalid interior quotes and backquotes are not validated. quadrant.md#strings: A quote followed by a backquote enters the markdown string context, which reads the characters up to the next backquote as a `markdown-string` unit and leaves at the backquote and the quote after it. The text holds no backquote and no quote: ``quadrant-1 "`a"b`"`` is rejected. A markdown string that is not closed makes the input rejected.

Reuse the plain double-quoted label form. quadrant.md#strings: `"` enters the string context, which reads all the characters up to the next `"` as a `string` unit, whose text is what lies between the quotes, and leaves the context at that `"`. quadrant.md#strings: A string has no escape, and a string that is not closed makes the input rejected.

Read a class selector as a separator and an element name. quadrant.md#the-class-name-context: `:::` enters the class name context, which reads one or more word characters of ASCII (letters, digits, and `_`) as a `class-name` unit and leaves; the `:` of the point follows it.

Read the point's colon and coordinate-list brackets. quadrant.md#the-point-context: A `:` and a `[` with whitespace around them enter the point context (rule 6 of the statement context); the whitespace is any whitespace character of [Notation](../common.md#notation), line feeds, U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029, U+3000, and U+FEFF included, so `A`, U+00A0, and `: [0.3, 0.6]`, and `A:`, U+3000, and `[0.3, 0.6]` are the point `A`. quadrant.md#the-point-context: The `,` after the first coordinate, with whitespace of any kind around it, is a `,` unit, and `]` with the spaces after it is a `]` unit, which leaves the context; whitespace of any kind after the `[` and before the `]` is allowed.

Read a coordinate as one numeric text unit, including its internal directives. quadrant.md#the-point-context: In the point context, a **coordinate** is a `coordinate` unit: `1`, or `0` optionally followed by one character other than a line feed, U+2028, and U+2029, and one or more digits. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read the separator between coordinates. quadrant.md#the-point-context: The `,` after the first coordinate, with whitespace of any kind around it, is a `,` unit, and `]` with the spaces after it is a `]` unit, which leaves the context; whitespace of any kind after the `[` and before the `]` is allowed.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.comma.mermaid

patterns.comment: Reuse native percent comments outside label text. quadrant.md#comments: A comment starts at `%%` where a unit starts in the statement context and runs to the end of its line, the line feed left out; it belongs to no unit.

Read a semicolon as a statement separator. quadrant.md#diagram-and-statements: The diagram is the header and then the lines, separated by line breaks and `;`; the first line starts right after the header.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.semicolon.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read unquoted axis, quadrant and point labels while preserving maximal word runs through directives. quadrant.md#texts: A **text** is the text of an axis, of a quadrant, and the name of a point. quadrant.md#the-statement-context: So a text without quotes is made of words, `-`, and whitespace. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.
patterns.name: string.unquoted.mermaid

quadrant-style-separators.comment: Read style colons and commas outside property values. quadrant.md#rejections-outside-the-grammar: A style is a name, a `:`, and a value, with whitespace around the `:` or not; a second `:` after the value, and what follows it, is allowed. quadrant.md#points: The styles are separated by `,`, with whitespace around it or not, and may follow the `]` with no space.

quadrant-style.comment: Read one style property name and its whole value, without numeric scopes inside the value. quadrant.md#rejections-outside-the-grammar: A style is a name, a `:`, and a value, with whitespace around the `:` or not; a second `:` after the value, and what follows it, is allowed. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.
